## Technical Workshops

**Purse seine data reporting workshop (Seychelles, 16-19 March 2026).** Eighteen participants from six CPCs reviewed statistical and ROS reporting requirements for purse seine fisheries, including catch and effort, discards, species interactions, size data and drifting floating objects. Discussions addressed reporting workflows, data validation and priorities for improving data quality (for more details, see [report](https://iotc.org/meetings/iotc-purse-seine-fisheries-reporting-workshop)).

**ROS reporting workshop for longline fisheries (Johannesburg, 26-29 May 2026).** Twelve participants from eight CPCs reviewed ROS data reporting requirements, observer datasets, historical reporting gaps and electronic monitoring. The workshop also considered standardised forms, validation tools and opportunities to improve the consistency of national submissions (for more details see [report](https://iotc.org/meetings/iotc-ros-reporting-workshop-longline-fisheries)).

**Gillnet data collection under the IOTC ROS (online seminar, 3-4 November 2026).** The seminar reviewed existing reporting requirements and national data collection initiatives, including alternative and crew-based observer approaches, and provided an opportunity to discuss harmonisation of gillnet observer data collection and reporting. A workshop report is under preparation.

## Participation in External Meetings and Workshops

The Data Section participated in technical exchanges concerning EU data reporting and coordination, the Indian Ocean shark research plan, bycatch data, and abandoned, lost or otherwise discarded fishing gear (ALDFG), among other subjects. These activities supported dialogue on data requirements, harmonisation and data quality. The individual meetings and contributions are summarised in **Appendix I**.
